images.title: Mirror the quarter twice
images.purpose: Show a 4 by 4 tile grid made by mirroring a top left quarter over two red lines, giving exactly two lines of symmetry.
images.composition: One square tile grid centred, two red lines crossing in the middle, plenty of white space around.
images.exact_structure: One 4 by 4 grid of 16 square tiles. Each tile is split by a diagonal into one teal #0072B2 triangle and one amber #E69F00 triangle. Two reddish purple #CC79A7 lines cross at the middle, one vertical, one horizontal, making 4 quarters of 2 by 2 tiles. Each quarter is the mirror picture of its neighbour over the red line. Top left quarter has a thick grey #6B7280 outline. Exactly 16 tiles, 2 lines.
labels: Each quarter is a mirror picture
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
quarters that are plain copies instead of mirror pictures, or diagonal mirror lines drawn
images.takeaway: Mirror a quarter over each red line to fill the grid with exactly two lines of symmetry.
images.description: A 4 by 4 grid of teal and amber triangle tiles with two red lines crossing at the middle; each quarter mirrors its neighbour.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at two neighbouring quarters and say how one is the mirror picture of the other.

image_decisions.why: Mirroring a quarter over two lines is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
